decisions.title: cacheWarming now defaults to idle: re-arm ce-workflow's cold-cache compaction around warms
decisions.rationale: Idle warming re-sends the prompt with a one-token output cap for up to 30 minutes between runs when Pi expects it to save money (pi-ai dist/cache-warming.js evaluateCacheWarming: 0.15 x missCost - warmCost >= $0.05). coldCacheCompactMinutes (work-models.ts) counts cache_warm usage entries as fresh, so after a warm the idle-compaction timer and the hub's compact-before-park (sessions.ts compactBeforePark) skip compaction and the next message waits for it. Rare today (about 345k prompt tokens on Opus 5.5, 270k on GPT-6.1 Sol, 86k on Fable 5.2), but the user chose to keep warming and re-arm compaction (Q-01), and to make the cold-cache threshold one setting at 70% of the auto-compact point. Steps CU-03 to CU-05.
decisions.verification: CU-03: node scripts/test-work-compaction-notifications.mjs passed (four mode thresholds, project override, clamping, command/status and turn_end). test_sensitivity caught default 70→60 at the 65% assertion, baseline/restored green. CU-04: same test passed, including immediate/20s-delayed final warms and input/turn cancellation; red before fix at idle-warm handler assertion. CU-05: node scripts/test-work-compaction-notifications.mjs and (in hub) node --test scripts/test-sessions.mjs passed; park ignores only idle warms, protects recent real requests/long TTL, and hub sends the exact park command. Red before fix at recent-real-request guard.

decisions.title: Anthropic message threads
decisions.rationale: Requests on api.anthropic.com send only new messages and continue a server-side thread; any changed prefix (compaction, tool list) sends the full request, and thread_not_found and similar rejections retry once as a new thread (pi-ai dist/api/anthropic-messages.js sendThreadRequest). Recent sessions show 6 thread_not_found fallbacks, each recovered. Claude pool account switches land in the same fallback. hub/src/cache-miss.ts reads usage fields only; usage reported under threads was not separately verified.

decisions.title: Inherit pi-goal recovery, stale-context, settings, and documentation fixes
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: keep pi-goal 0.54.8 package-owned and make no ce-workflow compatibility adapter. Verified project fit: ce-workflow's coexistence path only reads the canonical custom goal-state entry and sends public /goal pause and /goal resume commands; the installed persistence source still serializes data.goal under customType goal-state, and the public commands remain unchanged. Verified upstream evidence: the installed 0.54.8 README, managing-goals and settings references, package metadata, source, and captured 0.54.4-to-0.54.8 artifact show internal transient-stream classification, stale extension-context cancellation, menu/settings lifecycle, and documentation/build changes while preserving the coexistence surface. Benefit: pi-goal users receive safer recovery and lifecycle behavior without duplicate state ownership. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local adapter.

decisions.title: Runtime 0.7.12 to 0.7.14: Core 0.7.13 fixes and CLI lookup changes
decisions.rationale: Manifests move to 0.7.14. Core 0.7.13 drops data: URLs in Markdown, shares the layer runtime with swizzled copies, keeps light-dismiss Popovers open during an outside touch pan, and renders disabled submit Buttons as type=button while hydrating. Search ignores keywords that name another entry, component reads add an example-block pointer to errors, and theme.list adds meta.skippedThemes. In the watched Selector and theme paths, the Selector list now writes its entrance side itself after the overlay margin moves it (hooks.ts, usePopoverInternal writesEntranceSide), and the theme and icon registries are shared by every Core copy on one React (themeRegistry.ts sharedForReact); our foundation builds one Core copy per design, so neither changes a contract we rely on. None fixes a failure in our pinned 0.7.12 runtime. Per the ledger, a runtime bump is a separate pin, integrity and browser review.
